subject: Mathematics
questionText: lim (n→∞) Σ (r = 1 to n) r²/(n³ + n r²) equals
explanation: Write the term as (1/n)·(r/n)²/(1 + (r/n)²). As n → ∞ the sum becomes ∫₀¹ x²/(1 + x²) dx = ∫₀¹ [1 − 1/(1 + x²)] dx = 1 − π/4.

subject: Mathematics
questionText: The value of ∫₀^π x/(1 + sin x) dx is
explanation: Let I be the integral. Using x → π − x, I = ∫₀^π (π − x)/(1 + sin x) dx, so 2I = π∫₀^π dx/(1 + sin x). An antiderivative of 1/(1 + sin x) is tan x − sec x = (sin x − 1)/cos x (continuous on [0, π]), so ∫₀^π dx/(1 + sin x) = [0 − (−1)] − [0 − 1] = 2. Hence 2I = 2π and I = π.

subject: Mathematics
questionText: The number of non-negative integer solutions of x₁ + x₂ + x₃ = 10 with each xᵢ ≤ 4 is
explanation: Count solutions without the upper limit: C(12,2) = 66. Subtract those with some xᵢ ≥ 5: put yᵢ = xᵢ − 5, giving C(7,2) = 21 for each of 3 variables (63). Two variables ≥ 5 would need sum ≥ 10 with the third 0: C(2,2) = 1 for each of 3 pairs (add back 3). Total = 66 − 63 + 3 = 6.

subject: Mathematics
questionText: Three fair dice are thrown. The probability that the sum of the numbers shown is 10 is
explanation: The number of ordered triples (a,b,c) with 1 ≤ a,b,c ≤ 6 and a + b + c = 10 is 27. Probability = 27/216 = 1/8.

subject: Mathematics
questionText: The number of complex numbers z satisfying z⁵ = z̄ (conjugate of z) is
explanation: Taking moduli, |z|⁵ = |z|, so |z| = 0 or 1. z = 0 is one solution. If |z| = 1 then z̄ = 1/z, so z⁶ = 1, giving 6 more. Total = 7.

subject: Mathematics
questionText: The value of ∫₀¹ ln(1 + x)/(1 + x²) dx is
explanation: Put x = tan θ: I = ∫₀^(π/4) ln(1 + tan θ) dθ. Using θ → π/4 − θ, 1 + tan(π/4 − θ) = 2/(1 + tan θ), so I = ∫₀^(π/4) [ln 2 − ln(1 + tan θ)] dθ = (π/4) ln 2 − I. Hence I = (π/8) ln 2.

subject: Mathematics
questionText: The number of integer values of k for which x³ − 3x + k = 0 has three distinct real roots is
explanation: f(x) = x³ − 3x + k has a local maximum f(−1) = k + 2 and a local minimum f(1) = k − 2. Three distinct real roots need k + 2 > 0 and k − 2 < 0, i.e. −2 < k < 2. Integers: −1, 0, 1, so 3 values.

subject: Mathematics
questionText: The tangent to y = x³ at the point (1, 1) meets the curve again at
explanation: Tangent at (1,1): y = 3x − 2. Solving x³ = 3x − 2 gives x³ − 3x + 2 = (x − 1)²(x + 2) = 0. The other point is x = −2, y = −8.

subject: Mathematics
questionText: The number of 2 × 2 matrices with every entry 0 or 1 that are singular (determinant 0) is
explanation: There are 16 such matrices. det = ad − bc ≠ 0 needs exactly one of ad, bc to be 1: ad = 1, bc = 0 gives 3 cases; ad = 0, bc = 1 gives 3 cases. Non-singular = 6, so singular = 16 − 6 = 10.

subject: Mathematics
questionText: lim (x→0) (sin x − x)/(x tan² x) equals
explanation: sin x − x ≈ −x³/6 and x tan² x ≈ x³. The limit is −1/6.

subject: Physics
questionText: A block of mass m slides on the smooth inclined face (45°) of a wedge of mass M = m, which rests on a smooth horizontal floor. The acceleration of the wedge is
explanation: For a smooth block on a free smooth wedge, A = mg sinθ cosθ/(M + m sin²θ). With M = m and θ = 45°: A = g(1/2)/(1 + 1/2) = g/3.

subject: Physics
chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questionText: A uniform solid disc rolls without slipping down a rough incline of angle 30°. The minimum coefficient of static friction required is
explanation: For a disc a = (2/3)g sinθ and friction f = (1/3)mg sinθ. Need f ≤ μ mg cosθ, so μ_min = (1/3) tanθ = (1/3)(1/√3) = 1/(3√3) ≈ 0.19.

subject: Physics
questionText: The minimum energy needed to shift a satellite of mass m from a circular orbit of radius 2R to one of radius 3R around a planet of mass M is
explanation: Orbital energy E = −GMm/(2r). ΔE = −GMm/(6R) − (−GMm/(4R)) = GMm(1/4 − 1/6)/R = GMm/(12R).

subject: Physics
questionText: One mole of an ideal monatomic gas goes through the cycle (P₀,V₀) → (2P₀,V₀) → (2P₀,2V₀) → (P₀,2V₀) → (P₀,V₀). The efficiency of the cycle is
explanation: Net work = area of the rectangle = P₀V₀. Heat is absorbed in the first two steps: isochoric Q = (3/2)(2P₀V₀ − P₀V₀) = 1.5P₀V₀; isobaric Q = (5/2)(4P₀V₀ − 2P₀V₀) = 5P₀V₀. Q_in = 6.5P₀V₀, so η = 1/6.5 = 2/13 ≈ 15.4%.

subject: Physics
questionText: A capacitor charges through a resistor from a battery (time constant τ = RC). The time taken for the charge to reach three-fourths of its final value is
explanation: q = q₀(1 − e^(−t/τ)). Setting q = 3q₀/4 gives e^(−t/τ) = 1/4, so t = τ ln 4.

subject: Physics
questionText: A charged particle enters a uniform magnetic field with its velocity at 60° to the field. The ratio of the pitch of its helical path to the radius of the helix is
explanation: Radius r = mv sin60°/(qB) = √3mv/(2qB). Pitch p = v cos60° × 2πm/(qB) = πmv/(qB). p/r = π/(√3/2) = 2π/√3.

subject: Physics
questionText: A parallel beam of light falls on a glass sphere (μ = 1.5) of radius R. The beam converges at a point beyond the far surface of the sphere at a distance
explanation: First surface: 1.5/v − 1/∞ = 0.5/R gives v = 3R from the front surface, i.e. R beyond the back surface. Second surface (object virtual, u = +R): 1/v − 1.5/R = (1 − 1.5)/(−R), so 1/v = 2/R and v = R/2 beyond the far surface.

subject: Physics
chapter: Mechanical Properties of Solids and Fluids
questionText: A U-tube with horizontal base of length L contains liquid and is rotated with angular speed ω about a vertical axis passing through one of its arms. The difference in liquid levels in the two arms is
explanation: In the rotating frame the free surface follows y = ω²x²/(2g) measured from the axis. The arm on the axis is at x = 0 and the other at x = L, so Δh = ω²L²/(2g).

subject: Physics
questionText: A block of mass m hangs from a light string that passes over a pulley (a uniform disc of mass m and radius r, free to rotate) and is tied to a vertical spring of constant k. The string does not slip. The period of small oscillations is
explanation: Energy method: KE = ½mv² + ½(½mr²)(v/r)² = ½(3m/2)v². Effective mass = 3m/2, so T = 2π√(3m/(2k)).

subject: Chemistry
questionText: For N₂O₄(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g), Kp = 4 atm at a certain temperature. The degree of dissociation of N₂O₄ at a total pressure of 1 atm is
explanation: Kp = 4α²P/(1 − α²). With P = 1 atm: 4 = 4α²/(1 − α²), so α² = 1 − α², α² = 1/2 and α = 1/√2 ≈ 0.71.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: A decomposes by two parallel first-order paths: A → B (k₁) and A → C (k₂), with k₁ = 2k₂. The percentage of B in the products is
explanation: For parallel first-order reactions, [B]/[C] = k₁/k₂ = 2 at all times. So B = 2/3 of the products ≈ 66.7%.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: The number of geometrical isomers of the octahedral complex [Co(NH₃)₃Cl₃] is
explanation: An octahedral MA₃B₃ complex has two geometrical isomers: facial (fac) and meridional (mer). Neither is optically active.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: The total number of monochlorinated products (including stereoisomers) formed by free-radical chlorination of 2-methylbutane is
explanation: Four constitutional isomers form: 1-chloro-2-methylbutane (chiral, 2), 2-chloro-2-methylbutane (achiral, 1), 2-chloro-3-methylbutane (chiral, 2) and 1-chloro-3-methylbutane (achiral, 1). Total = 6.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: Benzenediazonium chloride reacts with phenol in mildly alkaline medium. The product is
explanation: This is an azo coupling. The phenoxide ion is attacked at the para position by the diazonium electrophile, giving p-hydroxyazobenzene, an orange dye.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: Among H₂O, H₂S, H₂Se and H₂Te, the strongest acid in water is
explanation: Down group 16 the H−E bond becomes longer and weaker, so H⁺ is released more easily. H₂Te is the strongest acid of the four.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: In a sample of hydrogen atoms, electrons are excited to n = 6. The maximum number of different spectral lines emitted as they return to the ground state is
explanation: Maximum lines = n(n − 1)/2 = 6 × 5/2 = 15.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: A mixture of ethanal and propanal is treated with dilute NaOH. The number of different aldol (β-hydroxy carbonyl) products, ignoring stereoisomers, is
explanation: Both aldehydes have α-hydrogens, so each can act as nucleophile (enolate) and as electrophile. Self-aldols: 2; cross-aldols: 2. Total = 4.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: Which of the following has the maximum number of lone pairs on the central atom?
explanation: Lone pairs on the central atom: XeF₂ = 3, ClF₃ = 2, SF₄ = 1, IF₅ = 1.

subject: Chemistry

subject: Physics
questionText: A conducting sphere of radius R carries charge +Q and is surrounded by a concentric thin shell of radius 2R carrying −Q. The potential of the inner sphere is (k = 1/4πε₀)
explanation: Potentials add: inner sphere contributes kQ/R at its own surface, and the shell contributes k(−Q)/(2R) everywhere inside it. V = kQ/R − kQ/(2R) = kQ/(2R).

subject: Physics
chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questionText: Photons emitted in the n = 2 → n = 1 transition of He⁺ fall on a metal of work function 4.8 eV. The stopping potential is
explanation: For He⁺ (Z = 2), E = 13.6 × 4 × (1 − 1/4) = 40.8 eV. K_max = 40.8 − 4.8 = 36 eV, so the stopping potential is 36 V.

subject: Physics
questionText: Two wires of the same material, with radii in the ratio 1 : 2, are joined end to end and kept under the same tension. The ratio of wave speeds in the thinner and thicker wires is
explanation: v = √(T/μ) and μ = ρπr², so v ∝ 1/r. v_thin/v_thick = 2/1.

subject: Physics
questionText: A uniform chain of length L lies on a smooth table with one-third of its length hanging over the edge. It is released from rest. Its speed when the last link leaves the table is
explanation: Take the table top as reference. Initially the hanging third (mass m/3) has its centre at L/6 below: U₁ = −mgL/18. Finally the whole chain hangs with centre at L/2: U₂ = −mgL/2. Loss = 4mgL/9 = ½mv², so v = √(8gL/9) = (2/3)√(2gL).

subject: Chemistry
questionText: The degree of unsaturation (double-bond equivalent) of a compound with molecular formula C₅H₈O is
explanation: DBE = (2C + 2 − H)/2 (oxygen is ignored) = (10 + 2 − 8)/2 = 2. Possible structures include cyclopentanone or a pent-3-en-2-one.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: The molarity of a "20 volume" hydrogen peroxide solution is about
explanation: 20 volume means 1 L of solution gives 20 L of O₂ at STP. 2H₂O₂ → 2H₂O + O₂, so 22.4 L O₂ comes from 2 mol H₂O₂ (i.e. 11.2 L from 1 mol). Molarity = 20/11.2 ≈ 1.79 M.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: The spin-only magnetic moment of [Fe(H₂O)₆]²⁺ is about
explanation: Fe²⁺ is 3d⁶ and H₂O is a weak-field ligand, so the complex is high spin with 4 unpaired electrons. μ = √(4 × 6) = √24 ≈ 4.90 BM.

subject: Chemistry
questionText: A zero-order reaction has a half-life of 20 min when the initial concentration is 0.4 M. The time needed for the concentration to fall from 0.4 M to 0.1 M is
explanation: For zero order, t½ = [A]₀/(2k), so k = 0.4/(2 × 20) = 0.01 M min⁻¹. Time = Δ[A]/k = 0.3/0.01 = 30 min.

subject: Mathematics
questionText: The number of real solutions of eˣ = x² is
explanation: Let f(x) = eˣ − x². For x > 0, f′(x) = eˣ − 2x > 0 (since eˣ ≥ ex > 2x), and f(0) = 1 > 0, so there is no positive root. For x < 0, f is continuous with f(−1) < 0 < f(0) and f is increasing there, giving exactly one root. Total = 1.

subject: Mathematics
questionText: The value of ∫₀^∞ x e^(−x²) dx is
explanation: Put u = x², du = 2x dx: ∫₀^∞ x e^(−x²) dx = ½∫₀^∞ e^(−u) du = ½.

subject: Mathematics
questionText: Two distinct numbers are chosen at random from 1, 2, …, 20. The probability that their sum is even is
explanation: The sum is even when both are odd or both are even: C(10,2) + C(10,2) = 45 + 45 = 90 out of C(20,2) = 190. Probability = 90/190 = 9/19.

subject: Mathematics
questionText: The maximum value of sin x + cos x + sin x cos x is
explanation: Let t = sin x + cos x ∈ [−√2, √2]; then sin x cos x = (t² − 1)/2. The expression is t + (t² − 1)/2, increasing for t > −1, so its maximum is at t = √2: √2 + (2 − 1)/2 = √2 + 1/2.
